provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Washing my hands
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state when to wash hands.
The pupils should be able to list steps of hand washing with soap.
Introduction:
We use our hands to touch many things.
Dirty hands can make us sick.
Content:
Wash hands before eating food.
Wash hands after using the toilet.
Wash hands after playing outside.
Steps for hand washing.
Wet hands with clean water.
Rub soap on hands.
Rub hands together for 20 seconds.
Rinse hands with clean water.
Dry hands with a clean towel.
Class activity:
Let us pretend to wash hands.
First wet your hands.
Now rub soap all over.
Evaluation questions:
When should we wash our hands?
What do we use to wash hands?
How many seconds should we rub soap?
Summary:
We wash our hands to stay clean and healthy.
Clean hands help us not get sick.

topics.title: Bathing every day
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify times to bathe.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate how to bathe.
Introduction:
We all get dirty during the day.
Bathing keeps us clean and fresh.
Content:
Bath in the morning before school.
Bath at night before bed.
Use soap to wash your body.
Use a sponge to scrub your skin.
Wash your hair with shampoo.
Dry your body with a towel.
Put on clean clothes after bath.
Class activity:
Let us pretend to bathe.
First wet your body.
Now rub soap all over.
Evaluation questions:
When do we bathe?
What do we use to bathe?
What do we do after bathing?
Summary:
Bathing every day keeps us clean and healthy.
Clean bodies feel good.

topics.title: Clean clothes
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify clean clothes.
The pupils should be able to sort dirty clothes.
Introduction:
Dirty clothes can make us itchy.
Clean clothes keep us healthy.
Content:
Wear a clean uniform to school every day.
Change your clothes after playing.
Put dirty clothes in the laundry basket.
Mum washes clothes with soap and water.
Sun dries clothes to kill germs.
Fold clean clothes and put them away.
Class activity:
Let us sort clothes into clean and dirty piles.
Here is a dirty shirt.
Where should it go?
Evaluation questions:
What should we wear to school?
Where do dirty clothes go?
What helps to clean clothes?
Summary:
Clean clothes keep us healthy and comfortable.
Dirty clothes need washing.

topics.title: Brushing my teeth
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state when to brush teeth.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate brushing teeth.
Introduction:
Teeth help us eat food well.
Clean teeth keep our mouth healthy.
Content:
Brush teeth in the morning after breakfast.
Brush teeth at night before bed.
Use a small amount of toothpaste.
Brush up and down on each tooth.
Brush the front and back of teeth.
Brush for two minutes.
Spit out toothpaste after brushing.
Class activity:
Let us pretend to brush teeth.
Hold your toothbrush.
Brush up and down.
Evaluation questions:
When do we brush our teeth?
How do we brush our teeth?
How long should we brush?
Summary:
Brushing teeth keeps them clean and strong.
Clean teeth help us eat well.

topics.title: Eating good food
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name healthy foods.
The pupils should be able to identify foods that help us grow.
Introduction:
Food gives us energy to play.
Some foods are healthier than others.
Content:
Fruits and vegetables help us grow.
Rice and yam give us energy.\ Beans help our muscles grow.
Drink milk for strong bones.
Drink water to stay fresh.
Eat less sugar and sweets.
Eat food from the four food groups.
Class activity:
Let us sort pictures into healthy and unhealthy foods.
This is a banana.
It is healthy.
Evaluation questions:
Name a healthy food.
What do fruits and vegetables do for us?
What should we drink to stay fresh?
Summary:
Good food helps us grow strong and healthy.
We should eat different kinds of food.

topics.title: Drinking clean water
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state why we drink water.
The pupils should be able to identify clean water sources.
Introduction:
Water is good for our bodies.
Dirty water can make us sick.
Content:
Water keeps our bodies fresh and cool.
Drink water when you are thirsty.
Drink clean water from the tap or well.
Use your own cup to drink water.
Wash your cup every day.
Drink water after playing outside.
Do not drink water from dirty places.
Class activity:
Let us pretend to drink water from our cups.
Pick up your cup.
Take a big sip.
Evaluation questions:
Why do we drink water?
Where should we get our water from?
What should we use to drink water?
Summary:
Clean water keeps us healthy and strong.
Always drink from your own cup.

topics.title: Sleep and rest
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify when to sleep.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate resting.
Introduction:
Our bodies need sleep to grow.
Rest helps us not get tired.
Content:
Sleep early at night to grow well.
Sleep for 10 to 12 hours every night.
Rest after playing outside.
Lie down quietly for rest time.
Close your eyes and be still.
Do not make noise when others are resting.
Wake up feeling fresh and happy.
Class activity:
Let us pretend to rest.
Lie down quietly on the mat.
Close your eyes and be still.
Evaluation questions:
When should we sleep?
What do we do after playing?
How do we feel after resting?
Summary:
Sleep and rest help us grow strong.
Rest makes us feel better.

topics.title: Using the toilet well
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state toilet rules.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate hand washing after toilet.
Introduction:
We all need to use the toilet.
We must be clean and careful.
Content:
Go to the toilet when you need to.
Sit properly on the toilet.
Do not play in the toilet.
Flush the toilet after use.
Wash hands with soap and water.
Dry your hands with a towel.
Tell a teacher if the toilet is dirty.
Class activity:
Let us pretend to use the toilet.
First sit on the toilet.
Now flush and wash hands.
Evaluation questions:
What do we do after using the toilet?
What do we use to flush the toilet?
Why do we wash our hands after toilet?
Summary:
Using the toilet well keeps us clean.
Always wash hands after using the toilet.

topics.title: Covering coughs
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate covering coughs.
The pupils should be able to identify why we cover coughs.
Introduction:
When we cough germs can go everywhere.
We must cover our coughs to keep friends safe.
Content:
Cough into your elbow not your hand.
Turn away from friends when you cough.
Use a tissue if you have one.
Throw used tissue in the bin.
Wash your hands after coughing.
If no tissue use your elbow.
Do not share food when coughing.
Class activity:
Let us practice coughing into our elbows.
Turn away from friends.
Cough into your elbow.
Evaluation questions:
Where should we cough?
Why do we cover our coughs?
What do we do after coughing?
Summary:
Covering coughs keeps germs away from friends.
We all stay healthy when we cover our coughs.

topics.title: Revision and hand wash practice
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list healthy habits.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate proper hand washing.
Introduction:
We have learned many healthy habits.
Let us practice them together.
Content:
Healthy habits keep us well.
We wash hands before eating.
We brush teeth morning and night.
We wear clean clothes every day.
 We bathe every day to stay clean.
We eat good food to grow strong.
We drink clean water to stay fresh.
We sleep early to grow well.
Class activity:
Let us practice hand washing together.
First wet your hands.
Now rub soap and count to 20.
Evaluation questions:
Name one healthy habit.
When should we wash our hands?
What helps us grow strong?
Summary:
All healthy habits help us stay well.
We will practice them every day.
